commits.subject: chore(web): keep one definition per server storage key
commits.body:
The saved-server migration read the legacy keys from its own copies of the
constants that storageKeys.ts already declared, so renaming a key there would
have silently broken the migration. The keys now live in serverProfiles.ts, the
only module that touches them, and the crash-recovery reset composes that list.

Saving a server also still wrote the old per-backend key. Nothing reads it since
saved profiles became the source of truth, and two profiles on the same backend
overwrote each other in it, so the write is gone.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: fix(web): tidy the saved-server controls on both layouts
commits.body:
The picker captioned itself with a `sr-only` span, but no rule ever hid it: the
caption rendered as stray text above the header. The select already carries an
accessible name, so the span is gone rather than hidden.

Sized to their labels, "Add server" and "Delete server" came out visibly
different widths, and the heading they sat in gave them whatever space the title
left, so they wrapped into a column that reached the modal's close button. They
are now equal columns as wide as the longer label, anchored to the last line of
the heading text, and a full row of equal halves once the heading stacks on a
phone.

Settings scrolled for a handful of pixels: the card padded content that pads
itself, drawing a frame inside a frame and spending 32px of an 85vh cap on
nothing. The card is now seamless and claims everything the backdrop margin
leaves, so the form fits without a scrollbar down to about 745px of viewport and
still scrolls when it genuinely does not fit.

A long server name pushed the app title into an ellipsis, so the picker takes a
share of the header bar instead of a width of its own, and drops to a row of its
own below 360px where 40% is not enough for both.

Deleting a saved server discarded a host, a username and a password on one
click. It now asks first, like deleting a session.
